Primal Pastures chicken breast: deep pink in color, raised on open pasture, corn-free, soy-free, foraging bugs, worms and insects and grown the way nature intended.
Conventionally raised chicken breast: pale, oversized, fatty and raised on corn and soy in confinement.
SEE THE DIFFERENCE ON THE PLATE

Primal Pastures vs.
Store Bought Organic Chicken

This is what chicken is supposed to look like. The one on the right is what you've been eating.

On the right is a conventionally raised chicken breast: pale, oversized, fatty and raised on corn and soy in confinement.

On the left is a Primal Pastures chicken breast: deep pink in color, raised on open pasture, corn-free, soy-free, foraging bugs, worms and insects and grown the way nature intended and fed a certified-organic, custom blended feed.

The color and texture speak for themselves. Our birds forage on open pasture every day, building healthy muscle and developing richer nutrients you can see and taste.

WHY IT MATTERS

What they eat becomes what you eat.
01
Open Pasture, Every Day

Not just "access to" outdoors. Our chickens are rotated to fresh pasture daily in their mobile coops and fed a custom blended certified-organic, corn and soy free feed.

02
No Corn, No Soy, No Seed Oils

Our chicken has been third party lab tested by Edacious and confirmed to be nutritionally superior to store-bought organic chicken, with 50% less PUFAs and 1000% more B Vitamins*

03
Regenerative, in action.

Soil regeneration is a loop. Animals nourish the soil, the soil grows rooted vegetation, the rooted vegetation nourishes the animals. Regeneration in action.

THE CLEANEST MEAT IN AMERICA

Meat that meets your standards.

Before factory farming, before feedlots, before corn and soy became the default, animals lived outside, ate what nature intended, and the meat was just better.

We've built Primal Pastures around that standard. Every animal on open pasture, every day. No shortcuts in the feed, no shortcuts on the land. Just real food, raised right, delivered to your door.

A NOTE FROM ROB

When my family and I started Primal Pastures in 2012, we had one goal: raise the cleanest meat for our own families. That mission has taken us across the country. 

A decade-plus later, we raise animals on open pasture the way they're meant to live and partner with regenerative farmers across America to ship that food directly to families who care where it comes from.

We hope you taste the difference. And if you ever have questions, please reach out. We love hearing from you.

Rob McDaniel

Founder, Primal Pastures

MURRIETA, CALIFORNIA

Transparency is the future of food, so nothing here is off-limits. No question is a bad question — and if you don't see yours below, reach out anytime at info@primalpastures.com.

Primal Pastures' grass fed steak and beef collection is sourced from cattle raised entirely on open pasture, no corn, no soy, no confinement. Every cut arrives 100% grass fed and grass finished, meaning the animals graze on fresh pasture from birth through harvest. Pasture-raising produces beef with a richer nutrient profile, including higher levels of omega-3 fatty acids and conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), compared with grain-finished alternatives. Whether you're looking for a ribeye, New York strip, sirloin, or ground beef, Primal Pastures ships fresh-frozen, pasture-raised beef directly to your door nationwide.

Why Grass Fed & Grass Finished Matters

Not all 'grass-fed' beef is the same. 'Grass-fed' simply means cattle grazed on grass at some point, but many conventional operations finish cattle on grain before slaughter. Primal Pastures beef is both grass fed and grass finished: our cattle graze on open pasture from birth through harvest, never entering a feedlot and never eating corn or soy.

This matters for three reasons:

Nutrition: Grass-finished beef typically carries a higher ratio of omega-3 to omega-6 fatty acids and elevated levels of conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) compared with grain-finished beef.
Flavor: A diet of varied pasture grasses produces beef with a more complex, mineral-forward flavor profile that many chefs and home cooks prefer.
Transparency: When you order from Primal Pastures, you know exactly how your beef was raised, pasture-raised in California, corn-free, soy-free, and delivered frozen directly to your door.
How to Choose the Best Grass Fed Steak

Not every cut suits every occasion. Here's a quick guide to the grass fed steaks in our collection:

Ribeye, Best for Rich Flavor

The ribeye's natural marbling makes it the most forgiving cut to cook and the most intensely beefy in taste. Ideal for cast-iron searing or grilling over high heat.

New York Strip, Best for Balance

The strip offers a firm texture with good marbling. It responds well to a dry-brine overnight and a hot sear, producing a crust that complements grass-fed beef's mineral-forward character.

Sirloin, Best for Everyday Cooking

Leaner than the ribeye and strip, sirloin is a versatile weeknight option. Because grass-finished beef is naturally leaner than grain-finished, avoid overcooking, medium-rare to medium delivers the best result.

Filet Mignon, Best for Tenderness

The most tender cut in the collection, with a mild flavor profile. Works best with simple preparations: tallow, salt, and high heat.

Ground Beef, Best for Versatility

Our grass fed ground beef is sourced from the same pasture-raised cattle as our steaks, making it an easy entry point for everyday meals.

About Our Corn & Soy Free Pasture Raised Chicken

Corn and soy free pasture raised chicken from Primal Pastures is raised entirely outdoors on open pasture, with no corn, no soy, and no synthetic additives in the feed. Our pastured chickens forage naturally on grass and insects, producing meat with a richer flavor profile and a healthier fat balance than conventionally raised birds.

Because we eliminate corn and soy, the two most common feed ingredients in commodity poultry, you get clean protein that fits ancestral, carnivore, and elimination-diet lifestyles. Every cut is hand-processed in small batches and shipped frozen directly to your door. Browse our full selection of pasture raised chicken below, from whole birds to individual cuts.

Why Corn & Soy Free Chicken Matters

Corn and soy are the most widely used ingredients in conventional poultry feed, and they come with tradeoffs. Corn is calorie-dense but high in omega-6 linoleic acid, which can skew the fat ratio in chicken meat toward inflammatory pathways when consumed in excess. Soy is the dominant protein source in commercial chicken diets, but it contains phytoestrogens and is one of the FDA's top nine major allergens, making it a concern for people with sensitivities or those following elimination diets.

Primal Pastures removes both corn and soy from the feed entirely. That matters whether you follow a carnivore protocol, an ancestral diet, a low-PUFA framework, or simply want to know exactly what your food ate. Third-party lab testing from Edacious Food Lab backs this up: our chicken tests at 51% fewer PUFAs and a 6:1 omega-6 to omega-3 ratio, compared to 12:1 for conventional chicken.

Our chicken is 100% pasture raised, corn and soy free, vaccine free, and all USA born, raised, and harvested.

How to Choose Your Pasture Raised Chicken Cut

All Primal Pastures chicken is corn and soy free and pasture raised, the difference between cuts comes down to cooking method, portion size, and flavor intensity.

Whole Chicken

Best for roasting, spatchcocking, or slow cooker meals. A whole bird delivers the best value per pound and is ideal for meal prepping multiple servings at once.

Chicken Thighs

Dark meat with higher fat content and deeper flavor. Thighs are forgiving to cook and stay moist in the oven, on the grill, or braised in a skillet.

Chicken Drumsticks

Economical, family-friendly, and excellent for grilling or baking. The bone-in format delivers rich collagen and flavor.

Chicken Breasts

Lean white meat with a mild flavor. Best cooked quickly over high heat or sliced for salads and stir-fries. Because our birds are pastured rather than factory farmed, the breasts remain naturally sized, not artificially enlarged.
